reasons: Overlaps on machine learning, robotics, reinforcement learning
subject: Interested in your robot learning work
body:
Hello Professor Finn,

My name is Vinil Polepalli and I am an undergraduate at New York University studying Computer Science and Business. I was a machine learning research intern at the Carnegie Mellon Robotics Institute, where I trained a PyTorch semantic segmentation model to 0.88 mean IoU and 0.94 F1 on 25,000 labeled aerial images and integrated it into an autonomous UAV pipeline running under 100 ms per frame.

I read MAML, and the part I find most useful is that it asks nothing of the architecture: optimizing for parameters a few gradient steps away from good on any task in the distribution covers classification, regression and policy learning alike. The cost that made this concrete for me was those 25,000 labels, which came from one project's flights, so a new species or site means labeling again. I would want to treat each species-site pair as a task and measure how few labeled tiles a MAML-initialized model needs to match what we got from the full set.

I would like to learn more about what the lab is working on now, and to understand where someone with this background could actually be useful to you.

In the past, I have worked on the following related projects:
- Semantic segmentation for UAV-based environmental monitoring at Carnegie Mellon Robotics Institute: 0.88 mean IoU and 0.94 F1 on 25,000 labeled aerial images, sub-100 ms inference across 30 flights
- Hsp90 inhibitor virtual screening in the Chiosis Lab at Memorial Sloan Kettering: 4,566 candidates screened at 0.984 GNN ROC AUC and 5x enrichment, 0 Lipinski violations in the top 50: https://hsp90-dashboard.vercel.app/
- Sole author, cVAE-augmented deep learning for pan-cancer RNA-seq classification, about 98% test accuracy across 5 cancer types on TCGA: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.02743

Outside of research I was invited to Y Combinator's Startup School, reached the VEX Robotics World Championship semifinals, and have qualified for the AIME three times.

I have extensively used PyTorch, OpenCV and Python in past work, but have a lot of coding experience and am adaptable to whichever libraries your lab utilizes. Please let me know if there is a fit in your lab.

I have attached my resume, and would be happy to elaborate on any of this.

Thank you!

--
Vinil Polepalli
New York University | Class of 2029
B.S. Computer Science and B.S. Business
